question.text: Which of the following expenses related to fund operations CANNOT be charged to the Category III AIF (i.e., must be borne by the Investment Manager itself)?

answer.text: Statutory audit fees of the AIF.
Investment Manager's office lease, travel expenses, and internal salary costs.
PPM audit fees and legal agreement drafting charges.

explanation.text: The Logic: The Category III AIF Managers workbook lists investment-management-function costs — including lease/rental, office maintenance, travel, outsourced support, investment due diligence, and transaction documentation for deal execution — as costs the manager must bear and which cannot be charged to the fund. Custodian fees, RTA charges, statutory audit fees, PPM audit fees, and legal-agreement drafting charges, by contrast, are described as fund-level set-up and operating expenses that can be charged to the AIF subject to the PPM. The Trap: Options A, B and D each look like internal overhead at first glance, but they are external service-provider costs that the workbook treats as legitimate fund expenses. The Investment Manager's own office, travel and salary costs are the items that must come out of its management fee. Note: The manager-borne cost list and the fund-level operating expense examples are taken from the Category III AIF Managers workbook (Series XIX-E).
